s1.syndrome_frame: febrile illness with skin lesions in an immunocompromised patient
salient_findings: tender annular erythematous plaques on the neck and trunk
violaceous and crusted centers with purpura and edematous rings
key_facts: tender lesions on the neck and trunk
recent chemotherapy with ixazomib, lenalidomide, and dexamethasone
skin biopsy showing inflammatory infiltrate of mononuclear cells
immunohistochemistry positive for CD68 and myeloperoxidase

raw.syndrome_frame: febrile illness with skin lesions in an immunocompromised patient
salient_findings: tender annular erythematous plaques on the neck and trunk
violaceous and crusted centers with purpura and edematous rings
key_facts: tender lesions on the neck and trunk
recent chemotherapy with ixazomib, lenalidomide, and dexamethasone
skin biopsy showing inflammatory infiltrate of mononuclear cells
immunohistochemistry positive for CD68 and myeloperoxidase

shortlist.label: Sweet syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: febrile illness with skin lesions and inflammatory infiltrate of mononuclear cells, consistent with Sweet syndrome

shortlist.label: Ecthyma gangrenosum
shortlist.why_kept: immunocompromised patient with fever and skin lesions, raising concern for ecthyma gangrenosum

shortlist.label: Leukocytoclastic vasculitis
shortlist.why_kept: skin lesions with purpura and inflammatory infiltrate, although no obvious leukocytoclastic vasculitis on biopsy

shortlist.label: Malignant pyoderma
shortlist.why_kept: skin lesions with violaceous and crusted centers, consistent with malignant pyoderma

shortlist.label: Pseudomonas aeruginosa sepsis
shortlist.why_kept: immunocompromised patient with fever and skin lesions, raising concern for pseudomonas sepsis

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of fever, tender lesions on the neck and trunk, and skin biopsy showing inflammatory infiltrate of mononuclear cells, along with immunohistochemistry positive for CD68 and myeloperoxidase, is consistent with Sweet syndrome, especially in the context of recent chemotherapy and a history of multiple myeloma.

rejected.label: Ecthyma gangrenosum
rejected.why: Negative blood culture and lack of obvious signs of Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection make this less likely

rejected.label: Leukocytoclastic vasculitis
rejected.why: Nuclear dust present without obvious leukocytoclastic vasculitis in the biopsy

rejected.label: Malignant pyoderma
rejected.why: Clinical presentation and biopsy findings do not align closely with this condition

rejected.label: Pseudomonas aeruginosa sepsis
rejected.why: Negative blood culture and clinical presentation not typical for Pseudomonas sepsis
